Article 43

(1) Every child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence as referred to in Article 36 letter g obtains rehabilitation services both physical and psychosocial.

(2) Forms of protection for child victims of acts of Violence in the form of basic social services, education, religious guidance, health services, psychological counseling and/or psychotherapy, legal assistance, recreational activities, educational and empowerment of parents of child victims of acts of violence.

(3) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from committing acts of Violence against Children.

Article 12

The Regional Government provides Women's Protection in the form of:

a. prevention of Violence against Women;
b. provision of services for Women victims of Violence that require regional level coordination; and
c. strengthening and developing institutions providing Women's Protection services.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration that leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Head of Region hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Tanah Bumbu Regency. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Tanah Bumbu Regency. 5. Office is a Regional Agency that administers governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. 6. Regional Agency is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs which are the authority of the Region. 7. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, thereby being able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into male and female. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights in order to live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not adequately met. 19. Child who becomes a victim of acts of Violence is a Child who experiences maltreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trusted namely parents, close relatives, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situations is a Child who is in a situation and condition that endangers himself such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who becomes a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous communities is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Child who is economically exploited is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others with or without being paid. 25. Child who is sexually exploited is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who becomes a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child growth and development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries with authority to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, Child in conflict with the law, Child from isolated indigenous communities, Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substances (Napza) abuse, Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, Child with special needs, and Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or deed that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transportation, transfer of a Child using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose and/or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 32.

Article 4

and Protection

The regulation concerning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of every Woman and Child to survival, growth and development;
b. improve the quality of life of Women, Children and family quality;
c. enhance the institutional capacity of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region, including the development of gender and Child data systems; and
d. provide protection for Women's rights and fulfillment of Children's Rights including Special Protection for Children from various forms of Violence and other discriminatory treatment.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND

CHILD PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The principal matters contained in the body of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection and Child Protection include:

a. Women's Empowerment;
b. Women's Protection;
c. Child Protection;
d. safe houses;
e. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by Village government;
f. family quality;
g. cooperation; h. awards;
i. Community participation;
j. financing;
k. prohibitions;

1. investigative provisions; and

m. criminal provisions.

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSE

Article 46

(1) Women and child victims of Violence who require continuous handling have the right to stay in a safe house.

(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a place or temporary safe shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored. (3) The operation and management of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(4) Further provisions regarding the operation of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 45

(1) Special Protection for child victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i is carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.

(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering to involve Children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 29

Legal assistance/expert witness support services as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d number 3 include:

a. ensuring the Child is accompanied by a legal companion; and b. facilitating assistance to Child victims of violence, both in the examination process in court proceedings and outside court proceedings.

Article 40

a. prevention and supervision for Children who are utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation;

Article 41

(1) Special Protection for child victims of narcotics abuse including scented glue sniffing and the like that can cause hallucinogenic effects and the like as referred to in Article 36 letter e, and involved in the use, production and distribution thereof, is carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation by the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from deliberately placing, allowing, involving, ordering to involve Children in the abuse, production and distribution of Narcotics, Scented Glue and the like as referred to in paragraph (1).

c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, labor unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation against Children.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation against Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Child who becomes a victim of acts of Violence is a Child who experiences maltreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trusted namely parents, close relatives, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. 1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The principal matters contained in the body of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection and Child Protection include:

a. Women's Empowerment;
b. Women's Protection;
c. Child Protection;
d. safe houses;
e. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by Village government;
f. family quality;
g. cooperation; h. awards;
i. Community participation;
j. financing;
k. prohibitions;

1. investigative provisions; and

m. criminal provisions.

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. CONCERNING

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The principal matters contained in the body of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection and Child Protection include:

a. Women's Empowerment;
b. Women's Protection;
c. Child Protection;
d. safe houses;
e. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by Village government;
f. family quality;
g. cooperation; h. awards;
i. Community participation;
j. financing;
k. prohibitions;

1. investigative provisions; and

m. criminal provisions.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Letter b

What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the basic rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Letter d

What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in carrying out the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women. Letter e

What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefits for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Letter f

What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Letter g

What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

Article 45

(1) Special Protection for child victims of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 36 letter i is carried out through supervision, prevention, treatment and rehabilitation.

(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from placing, allowing, involving, ordering to involve Children in situations of mistreatment and neglect as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 42

(1) Special Protection for child victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f is carried out through efforts of supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration by the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations takes steps in the form of:

a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with legislation.
(3) Protection for child victims of Child Trafficking is implemented through Shelter Houses and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referral from government agencies or the Community.
(4) Every child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment as well as the Community.

Article 40

(1) Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d is carried out through:

a. prevention and supervision for Children who are utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation;
b. disseminating and/or socializing legislation related to the Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, labor unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation against Children.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation against Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 44

(1) Special Protection for Children with special needs as referred to in Article 36 letter h is carried out through efforts to:

a. treat Children humanely in accordance with the dignity and Rights of Children;
b. fulfill special needs; and
c. obtain the same treatment as other Children to achieve social integration as fully as possible and individual development.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from treating Children with special needs in a discriminatory manner, by ignoring their views including labeling and equalization in education for Children with special needs.

Article 39

(1) Special Protection for Children from remote indigenous communities as referred to in Article 36 letter c is carried out through the provision of facilities and infrastructure to be able to enjoy their own culture, recognize and practice their own religious teachings, and use their own language.

(2) Every person and/or and/or any parties are prohibited from obstructing Children as referred to in paragraph (1) from enjoying their own culture, recognizing and practicing their religious teachings, and using their own language without neglecting access to Community and cultural development.

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, existing Regional policies regarding Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Region shall remain in effect, insofar as they do not conflict with this Regional Regulation.

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The principal matters contained in the body of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection and Child Protection include:

a. Women's Empowerment;
b. Women's Protection;
c. Child Protection;
d. safe houses;
e. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by Village government;
f. family quality;
g. cooperation; h. awards;
i. Community participation;
j. financing;
k. prohibitions;

1. investigative provisions; and

m. criminal provisions.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Letter b

What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the basic rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Letter d

What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in carrying out the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women. Letter e

What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefits for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Letter f

What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Letter g

What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

Article 48

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to improve family quality in the form of:

a. improving family quality in realizing gender equality and Children's Rights.
b. strengthening and developing service provider institutions for improving family quality in realizing gender equality and Children's Rights whose working area is within the Region.
c. providing services for families in realizing gender equality and Children's Rights whose working area is within the Region.
(2) Provisions regarding the procedures for improving family quality as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER VII SAFE HOUSE

Article 46

(1) Women and child victims of Violence who require continuous handling have the right to stay in a safe house.

(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a place or temporary safe shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored. (3) The operation and management of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(4) Further provisions regarding the operation of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 40

(1) Special Protection for Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually as referred to in Article 36 letter d is carried out through:

a. prevention and supervision for Children who are utilized by certain parties as objects of exploitation;
b. disseminating and/or socializing legislation related to the Protection of Children who are exploited economically and/or sexually;
c. monitoring, reporting and imposing sanctions; and
d. involving various government agencies, companies, labor unions, NGOs, and the Community in the elimination of exploitation against Children.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from conducting economic and/or sexual exploitation against Children as referred to in paragraph (1).

Article 42

(1) Special Protection for child victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f is carried out through efforts of supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration by the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations takes steps in the form of:

a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with legislation.
(3) Protection for child victims of Child Trafficking is implemented through Shelter Houses and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referral from government agencies or the Community.
(4) Every child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment as well as the Community.

CHAPTER VIII

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND

CHILD PROTECTION BY VILLAGE GOVERNMENT

Article 47

(1) The Village Government implements Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in the Village.

(2) The implementation of Women's Empowerment and

Child Protection regulated in this Regional Regulation, applies mutatis mutandis in the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by

the Regional Government in accordance with the provisions of legislation.

(3) Funding for the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) is charged to the Village revenue and expenditure budget.

(4) Further provisions regarding the implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by the Regional Government are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights in order to live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not adequately met. 19. Child who becomes a victim of acts of Violence is a Child who experiences maltreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trusted namely parents, close relatives, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situations is a Child who is in a situation and condition that endangers himself such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who becomes a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous communities is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Child who is economically exploited is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others with or without being paid. 25. Child who is sexually exploited is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who becomes a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child growth and development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries with authority to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, Child in conflict with the law, Child from isolated indigenous communities, Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substances (Napza) abuse, Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, Child with special needs, and Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or deed that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transportation, transfer of a Child using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose and/or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 32.

Article 42

(1) Special Protection for child victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking as referred to in Article 36 letter f is carried out through efforts of supervision, protection, prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and reintegration by the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) To implement prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) the Regional Government together with the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Community, NGOs and Social Organizations takes steps in the form of:

a. conducting socialization and/or campaigns on the prevention, handling and elimination of Child Trafficking practices;
b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with legislation.
(3) Protection for child victims of Child Trafficking is implemented through Shelter Houses and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referral from government agencies or the Community.
(4) Every child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment as well as the Community.

CONCERNING

CHILD PROTECTION

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The principal matters contained in the body of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection and Child Protection include:

a. Women's Empowerment;
b. Women's Protection;
c. Child Protection;
d. safe houses;
e. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by Village government;
f. family quality;
g. cooperation; h. awards;
i. Community participation;
j. financing;
k. prohibitions;

1. investigative provisions; and

m. criminal provisions.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Letter b

What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the basic rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Letter d

What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in carrying out the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women. Letter e

What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefits for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Letter f

What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Letter g

What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

Article 44

(1) Special Protection for Children with special needs as referred to in Article 36 letter h is carried out through efforts to:

a. treat Children humanely in accordance with the dignity and Rights of Children;
b. fulfill special needs; and
c. obtain the same treatment as other Children to achieve social integration as fully as possible and individual development.
(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from treating Children with special needs in a discriminatory manner, by ignoring their views including labeling and equalization in education for Children with special needs.

Article 41

(1) Special Protection for child victims of narcotics abuse including scented glue sniffing and the like that can cause hallucinogenic effects and the like as referred to in Article 36 letter e, and involved in the use, production and distribution thereof, is carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation by the Regional Government and the Community.

(2) Every person and/or any party is prohibited from deliberately placing, allowing, involving, ordering to involve Children in the abuse, production and distribution of Narcotics, Scented Glue and the like as referred to in paragraph (1).

(1) Women and child victims of Violence who require continuous handling have the right to stay in a safe house.

(2) The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) provides a place or temporary safe shelter for victims of Violence until their rights are restored. (3) The operation and management of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that performs functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

(4) Further provisions regarding the operation of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Letter h

Letter i

What is meant by "gender responsive" is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers to achieve gender equality.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tanah Bumbu Regency. 2. Regional Government is the head of the Region as an element of the Regional Government administration that leads the implementation of governmental affairs which are the authority of the autonomous Region. 3. Women's Empowerment is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that Women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, thereby being able to build capacity and self-concept. 8. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into male and female. 9. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman. 10. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age including a Child who is still in the womb. 11. Child in conflict with the law (ABH) is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child who is a victim of a criminal act and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 12. Violence is any act that results in suffering or hardship physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 13. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting Women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights in order to live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from Violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security. 16. Toddler is a Child aged 0 (zero) to 5 (five) years, in the early stages of human development. 17. School-Age Child is a Child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 18. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs for mental and religious guidance as well as clothing, food, shelter, health, education, physical, and social services are not adequately met. 19. Child who becomes a victim of acts of Violence is a Child who experiences maltreatment such as being abused, humiliated, which endangers the Child physically, mentally and socially. 20. Child maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over children, who should be trusted namely parents, close relatives, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions (World Health Organization). 21. Child in emergency situations is a Child who is in a situation and condition that endangers himself such as a Child victim of riots, a Child who becomes a refugee, a Child victim of natural disasters and a Child in armed conflict. 22. Child in conflict with the law is a Child in conflict with the law, a Child victim of a criminal act, and a Child who is a witness to a criminal act. 23. Child of isolated indigenous communities is a Child who lives in a situation of isolation where they cannot access basic needs. 24. Child who is economically exploited is a Child who is forced and/or deceived to be employed by parents or others with or without being paid. 25. Child who is sexually exploited is the use of a Child for sexual purposes with cash or other forms of compensation between the Child, buyer of sexual services, intermediary or agent and other parties who profit from the sexual trade of the Child. 26. Child who becomes a victim of Napza abuse is a Child who suffers from dependence on Napza caused by Napza abuse, either by their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 27. Child with special needs is a Child who experiences physical and/or mental obstacles that interfere with their growth and development in accordance with the stages of Child growth and development. 28. Child victim of maltreatment is a Child who receives treatment that is not in accordance with the rights of the Child. 29. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries with authority to regulate and manage Government affairs, the interests of the local Community, based on Community initiative, rights of origin, and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the Government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia. 30. Child in need of Special Protection is a Child in emergency situations, Child in conflict with the law, Child from isolated indigenous communities, Child who is economically and/or sexually exploited, Child victim of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other active substances (Napza) abuse, Child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, Child victim of physical and/or psychological Violence, Child with special needs, and Child victim of maltreatment and neglect. 31. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or deed that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transportation, transfer of a Child using Violence or threat of violence, fraud, kidnapping, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of a position of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose and/or resulting in the exploitation of the Child. 32.

b. conducting cooperation with other Regions as well as with other countries through bilateral or multilateral cooperation in accordance with legislation.
(3) Protection for child victims of Child Trafficking is implemented through Shelter Houses and/or other Child Protection Institutions, through referral from government agencies or the Community.
(4) Every child victim of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, has the right to obtain treatment and rehabilitation both physical, psychological and reintegration in the family environment as well as the Community.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect for human rights is that the protection and empowerment of women is carried out as a manifestation of respect for women as part of Human Rights.

Letter b

What is meant by "gender equality" is one of the basic rights as a human being, the right to live with dignity, free from fear and free to determine life choices is not only intended for men, women also have the same rights in essence.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward Children by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups, and the condition of the Child.

Letter d

What is meant by "justice and legal certainty is that in carrying out the protection and empowerment of women it is based on justice and legal certainty of equality between men and women. Letter e

What is meant by "benefit" is providing the widest possible benefits for children and women for the interests of society, nation and state.

Letter f

What is meant by "participatory" is that every member of society is encouraged to play an active role in the decision-making process and implementation of child protection and women's empowerment, either directly or indirectly.

Letter g

What is meant by "the best interests of the Child" is that in all actions concerning Children carried out by the Regional Government, parents/family, and the Community, the best interests of the Child must be the primary consideration.

CONCERNING

1. GENERAL

In order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The drafting of the Regional regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection has the intent and purpose as the implementation of the widest possible regional autonomy, thus the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection sector is one sector that is quite important to be managed and regulated in order to realize Women who are capable physically, mentally, spiritually, socially, in knowledge, and skills so that they are ready to be empowered, as well as efforts to protect Women and Children from all acts of Violence in order to achieve the goal of welfare through a draft Regional regulation that can become a reference for all parties related to Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

The establishment of this Regional regulation is based on the principles of good legislative drafting and the principles of the material content of legislation.

The implementation of governmental affairs in the field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to increase efforts to Protect Women's rights, fulfill Children's Rights and Special Protection for Children and increase the role of Regional Government and the business sector, media and the Community in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection. The principal matters contained in the body of the Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Protection and Child Protection include:

a. Women's Empowerment;
b. Women's Protection;
c. Child Protection;
d. safe houses;
e. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection by Village government;
f. family quality;
g. cooperation; h. awards;
i. Community participation;
j. financing;
k. prohibitions;

1. investigative provisions; and

m. criminal provisions.
